workedExamples.question_text: Write $\sec\alpha$, $\operatorname{cosec}\alpha$ and $\cot\alpha$ in terms of the primary trigonometric functions, stating when each reciprocal expression is valid.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\sec\alpha=\dfrac{1}{\cos\alpha}$ when $\cos\alpha\ne0$.

$\operatorname{cosec}\alpha=\dfrac{1}{\sin\alpha}$ when $\sin\alpha\ne0$.

$\cot\alpha=\dfrac{1}{\tan\alpha}$ when tangent is defined and nonzero, so both $\sin\alpha\ne0$ and $\cos\alpha\ne0$.

The definition $\cot\alpha=\dfrac{\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha}$ also applies when $\cos\alpha=0$, provided $\sin\alpha\ne0$.

Relative to $\alpha$, the opposite side is $6$, the adjacent side is $8$ and the hypotenuse is $10$.

$\begin{align*}\operatorname{cosec}\alpha&=\dfrac{\text{hyp}}{\text{opp}}\\&=\dfrac{10}{6}\\&=\dfrac53\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}\sec\alpha&=\dfrac{\text{hyp}}{\text{adj}}\\&=\dfrac{10}{8}\\&=\dfrac54\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}\cot\alpha&=\dfrac{\text{adj}}{\text{opp}}\\&=\dfrac86\\&=\dfrac43\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text:
Find the requested exact reciprocal ratio in each right-angled triangle.

(a) Relative to acute angle $\theta$, the hypotenuse is $26$ and the adjacent side is $10$. Find $\operatorname{cosec}\theta$.

(b) Relative to acute angle $\beta$, the opposite side is $9$ and the adjacent side is $40$. Find $\sec\beta$.

Without using a calculator, find the exact values of:

(a) $\sec150^\circ$

(b) $\operatorname{cosec}225^\circ$

(c) $\cot\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) The reference angle is $30^\circ$. Cosine is negative in quadrant II.

$\cos150^\circ=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

$\begin{align*}\sec150^\circ&=\dfrac{1}{\cos150^\circ}\\&=-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt3}\\&=-\dfrac{2\sqrt3}{3}\end{align*}$

(b) The reference angle is $45^\circ$. Sine is negative in quadrant III.

$\sin225^\circ=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$.

$\begin{align*}\operatorname{cosec}225^\circ&=\dfrac{1}{\sin225^\circ}\\&=-\sqrt2\end{align*}$

(c) The reference angle is $\dfrac\pi3$. Tangent is negative in quadrant IV.

$\tan\dfrac{5\pi}{3}=-\sqrt3$.

$\begin{align*}\cot\dfrac{5\pi}{3}&=\dfrac{1}{\tan(5\pi/3)}\\&=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\\&=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{3}\end{align*}$

Add one full turn to find an angle with the same terminal arm.

$-\dfrac\pi3+2\pi=\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$.

The reference angle is $\dfrac\pi3$. Tangent is negative in quadrant IV, so $\tan\dfrac{5\pi}{3}=-\sqrt3$.

$\begin{align*}\cot\left(-\dfrac\pi3\right)&=\cot\dfrac{5\pi}{3}\\&=\dfrac{1}{\tan(5\pi/3)}\\&=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\\&=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{3}\end{align*}$

foundation.question_text: State which primary trigonometric ratio is the reciprocal of $\sec\theta$.
State which primary trigonometric ratio is the reciprocal of $\operatorname{cosec}\theta$.

A right-angled triangle has opposite side $9$, adjacent side $12$ and hypotenuse $15$ relative to an acute angle $\theta$.
Find the exact value of $\sec\theta$.

A right-angled triangle has opposite side $20$, adjacent side $21$ and hypotenuse $29$ relative to an acute angle $\theta$.
Find the exact value of $\operatorname{cosec}\theta$.
Explain why $\sec 90^{\circ}$ is undefined using the unit circle definition.
foundation.solution_text:
On the unit circle, $\sec\theta=\dfrac{1}{x}$.
At $\theta=90^{\circ}$, the $x$-coordinate is $0$.
Division by $0$ is undefined, so $\sec 90^{\circ}$ is undefined.

development.question_text:
A right-angled triangle has an adjacent side of length $8$ and a hypotenuse of length $17$ for an acute angle $\theta$.
Find the exact value of $\operatorname{cosec}\theta$.

A right-angled triangle has opposite side $7$ and adjacent side $24$ relative to an acute angle $\beta$.
Find the exact value of $\sec\beta$.

State whether $\operatorname{cosec} 180^{\circ}$ is defined.
If so, state its value; if not, explain why.
Evaluate $\cot 90^{\circ}$ using the coordinate definition $\cot\theta=\dfrac{x}{y}$ on the unit circle.
development.solution_text:
At $\theta=90^{\circ}$, the coordinates on the unit circle are $(x,y)=(0,1)$.
$\cot 90^{\circ}=\dfrac{x}{y}=\dfrac{0}{1}=0$

mastery.question_text: Find the exact values of $\cot\pi$, $\cot\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$ and $\cot2\pi$, stating when a value is undefined.
mastery.solution_text:
On the unit circle, $\cot\theta=\dfrac{x}{y}$.
At $\theta=\pi$, $(x,y)=(-1,0)$, so $\cot\pi$ is undefined.
At $\theta=\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$, $(x,y)=(0,-1)$, so $\cot\dfrac{3\pi}{2}=\dfrac{0}{-1}=0$.
At $\theta=2\pi$, $(x,y)=(1,0)$, so $\cot2\pi$ is undefined.
